clue.text: Number in favour of being heard

indicators.note: something being heard is only listened to, so the word wanted is the one that sounds the same, not the one spelt

parts.note: to be in favour of something is to be for it

explanation.surface: A figure that is popular when spoken about, or a vote in favour being announced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in favour of' is FOR, and FOR said out loud is the same as the number between three and five.
explanation.definitionFit: Four is a counting figure, so it is simply one example of a whole number.

clue.text: Safety device from America with iron casing

indicators.note: a casing is an outer shell wrapped around something, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
US is the usual abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: An imported American safety gadget housed in an iron shell.
explanation.walkthrough: The iron symbol splits round the American abbreviation: F, then US, then E.
explanation.definitionFit: A fuse is a thin wire in a circuit that melts and breaks the current to prevent overload and fire.

clue.text: Mentor working in Oxford college

indicators.note: something working is in motion and being moved about, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tutor employed at one of the Oxford colleges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' reads as a job description for the mentor, but it is the signal to rearrange the six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Merton is one of the oldest colleges of the University of Oxford, founded in the thirteenth century.

clue.text: Astronomer has front of telescope crushed by rod — gosh!

indicators.note: something crushed by another is squeezed inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a pole is a long rod

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of telescope
'My!' is an exclamation of surprise, like 'Gosh!'

explanation.surface: A stargazer's telescope gets smashed by a rod, and someone exclaims in dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: The T goes inside the rod word after its first letter, and the exclamation is tacked on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Ptolemy was the Greek-Egyptian scholar of Alexandria whose Earth-centred model of the heavens dominated for centuries.

clue.text: Chap, superior friend using hands

parts.note: a chap is a man
U stands for upper class, socially superior
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A man and his posh companion doing things by hand.
explanation.walkthrough: U meaning upper class or socially acceptable is a crossword favourite for 'superior' or 'posh'.
explanation.definitionFit: Manual comes from the Latin for hand, so doing something manually means doing it by hand rather than machine.

clue.text: Dangerous animals close? Cor, I'd get excited!

indicators.note: excited things are agitated and stirred up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone spots dangerous beasts nearby and gasps with thrilled alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like part of the scene, the animals being near, but it is fodder; 'Cor' is a British exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Crocodiles are large predatory reptiles with powerful jaws, an obvious example of beasts that can kill people.

clue.text: Young creatures always invading rented properties

indicators.note: an invader goes into territory, so one piece enters the middle of the other

parts.note: lets are properties rented out
ever means always, as in 'for ever'

explanation.surface: Baby animals keep moving into holiday rentals.
explanation.walkthrough: A let is the British term for a property rented out; the word for always splits it after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A leveret is a hare in its first year, so the plural names a group of young animals.

clue.text: Greek character features in second statue maybe

indicators.note: something that features in another appears within it, so one piece is set inside

parts.note: a second is a brief moment
nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek figure appears in a second sculpture, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a person in a statue, but it is a letter of the Greek alphabet, placed after the first two letters of the time word.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is one kind of monument, a structure put up to commemorate someone, hence the 'maybe' marking an example.

clue.text: Nests, as seen across one of the Great Lakes

indicators.note: a thing seen across another stretches over both its sides, so it surrounds it

parts.note: taken as written
Lake Erie is one of the five Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: Birds' nests spotted on the far shore of a Great Lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' looks like a link word but it is the two-letter wrapper round the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerie (or eyrie) is the high nest of an eagle or other bird of prey, so these are particular nests.

clue.text: Minister is nosy — start of trouble

parts.note: someone who pries is being nosy

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of trouble

explanation.surface: A clergyman's curiosity is the beginning of trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is nosy' has to be read as one verb phrase, a third-person verb meaning snoops.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister of religion is a member of the clergy, and a priest is one such ordained cleric.

clue.text: One church that is very cold

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for a noun: something that is very cold

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A single church building that is freezing inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' looks like it belongs to the church, describing it; it starts the definition instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen water is the standard example of a substance at freezing temperature, so it fits the description.

clue.text: Awkward uncle had to be got going

indicators.note: something awkward is clumsy and out of place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clumsy uncle had to be pushed into action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awkward' seems to describe the uncle, but it signals rearranging the letters of the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To launch a project or a ship is to set it in motion, so launched means started off.

clue.text: Some modest piece of poetry

indicators.note: some of something is only a part of it, so the letters are a portion of the next word

parts.note: the second to fourth letters

explanation.surface: A small, unassuming bit of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'modest', after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyric poem, usually addressed to a person or thing in an elevated style.

clue.text: Prime team?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a number divisible only by itself and one

definitions.note: 'Prime' is an adjective standing for a prime number, a noun
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a side in football or cricket, which fields this many players

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it seems to describe a top-quality team; separately, one word names a prime number and a sports side.
explanation.definitionFit: The number after ten is prime, and football and cricket sides are called by that number of players.

clue.text: The Spanish female is a little troublemaker

parts.note: el is Spanish for 'the'
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A Spanish woman turns out to be a small mischief-maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Spanish female' reads as one person, but it splits into the Spanish article and an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Elves in folklore are small, often mischievous sprites who play tricks on humans.

clue.text: Vehicle naughty laddies wrecked

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: naughty things misbehave and will not stay in order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Badly behaved boys trashed a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' looks like the anagram signal at the end, but it is the definition; 'naughty' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: To vandalise is to deliberately damage property, so a vandalised thing has been smashed up on purpose.

clue.text: Illnesses sending mum to the loo

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mum
the ladies is a women's toilet

explanation.surface: Stomach bugs keep making mother rush to the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the ladies' is the women's public toilet, and 'loo' is everyday British slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A malady is a disease or ailment, a slightly formal synonym for an illness.

clue.text: European conclusion being reported

indicators.note: a report is spoken out, so the word wanted only sounds like the one clued

parts.note: a conclusion is a finish or end

explanation.surface: The end of a European story is announced on the news.
explanation.walkthrough: The extra N is silent, so the word for an ending sounds exactly like the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: Finland is a Nordic country, so someone or something from there is one example of a European.

clue.text: Agreement is sealed by Italian, one wanting perfection

indicators.note: something sealed by another is shut up inside it, so one piece is wrapped by the other

parts.note: It is the abbreviation for Italian
a deal is an agreement
taken as written

explanation.surface: A contract is signed off by an Italian who insists on everything being flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' looks like a verb in the surface but is a piece: it joins the agreement word before both go inside the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An idealist pursues lofty principles and standards, typically aiming for a flawless state of things.

clue.text: Siren yet to disturb peace

indicators.note: to disturb things is to mess up their arrangement, so the letters are moved around

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An alarm that has not yet gone off to break the quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a wailing alarm breaking the calm; the calm itself is the answer, built from its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Serenity is a state of calm tranquillity, which is a close synonym of peace.

clue.text: Something hairy not far from the viewer

definitions.text: Something hairy not far from the viewer

parts.words: Something hairy not far from the viewer
parts.note: surface reading: a shaggy object or creature standing close to someone watching
setter's reading: the viewer is the organ of sight itself, and the hairy thing grows at its edge

explanation.walkthrough: The viewer seems to be a person or a television watcher, but it is the organ that does the viewing.
explanation.definitionFit: Short hairs fringe each eyelid, protecting the organ of sight, so they sit right beside it.

clue.text: The fellow with name for a bird

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a fellow
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A man who has a nickname for a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The male pronoun plus a one-letter abbreviation makes a female creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen is a female chicken, or the female of any bird species.

clue.text: Stuck in this place with tot running around

indicators.note: to run around something is to circle it, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to tot up is to add
here means in this place

explanation.surface: Trapped at home with a toddler racing about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a small child, but here it is the verb meaning sum up.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick fast to something, so adhered is the past tense of stuck.

clue.text: Society girl, a right leftie getting banned

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a young woman entering high society
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right
a red is a left-winger or communist

explanation.surface: A posh girl with radical politics is being excluded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' and 'leftie' sit side by side as political opposites, but one is just a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To be debarred is to be officially excluded or prohibited from something, a synonym for banned.

clue.text: Italian union facing examination

parts.note: TU is the abbreviation for trade union
a scan is a medical examination

explanation.surface: An Italian trade union confronts an inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian' reads as describing the union, but it is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuscany is an Italian region around Florence, so a Tuscan is one kind of Italian.

clue.text: Most reliable mate finally breaking confidence

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so one piece goes in the middle

parts.note: trust is confidence in someone

indicators.note: what comes finally is at the end, so only the closing letter is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of mate

explanation.surface: The most dependable friend ends up betraying a secret.
explanation.walkthrough: The single letter slips into the confidence word between its third and fourth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: True can mean loyal and dependable, so its superlative means the most faithful or reliable.

clue.text: Signal given by letter audibly

indicators.note: audibly means out loud, so the word wanted is spelt differently from what is heard

parts.note: the seventeenth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A signal passed on in writing and spoken aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' looks like a written message, but it means a letter of the alphabet, one that is pronounced like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre a cue is a prompt telling an actor when to speak or enter, so it is a signal.

clue.text: That girl's father is half cut

indicators.note: having half cut away means losing half the letters, so the front three are removed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl's dad is tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half cut' is British slang for drunk, which makes the surface; here it removes the first half of the six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive pronoun for a female, as in 'her book', means belonging to that girl.

clue.text: Joining up of everyone that is kept outside African party

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: a thing kept outside another forms its outer layer, so it wraps around the other

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for 'that is'
the ANC is the African National Congress, South Africa's governing party

explanation.surface: Everyone uniting, except an African political party that is excluded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept outside' sounds like exclusion of the party, but it means the abbreviation goes round the party.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a union formed for mutual benefit, so it is the act or result of joining together.

clue.text: University exceptionally stern as the result of disturbance

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university

indicators.note: exceptionally means in an unusual way, so the letters take an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A university becomes unusually strict after student protests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exceptionally stern' reads as very strict, but 'exceptionally' is telling you to rearrange the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrest is agitation or turmoil among people, so it is a close synonym of disturbance.

clue.text: Grass when you have hunger? Not good!

indicators.note: 'not' says something is absent, so the letter it names is taken away

parts.note: greed is a hunger for more
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Eating grass when you are starving is no good at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not good!' looks like an exclamation of disapproval but asks you to drop one letter from the hunger word.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeds are tall water-loving plants of the grass family, so a reed is a kind of grass.

clue.text: Sailor perched when traversing lake

indicators.note: a thing traversing another stretches across it end to end, so it spans round the other

parts.note: to have perched is to have sat
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A sailor sits up on deck as the boat crosses a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: An old salt is an experienced seaman, a common informal word.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt, short for old salt, is an informal word for a seasoned mariner, from the salt sea.

clue.text: Agreement was sentimental to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent means only partly, so just a portion of the words is used

parts.note: the letters run from the second letter of the first word into the second word

explanation.surface: A deal that was a little soppy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to some extent' looks like it softens 'sentimental', but it marks the answer as sitting inside the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Assent is formal consent or approval, so giving it means expressing acceptance.

clue.text: Wind — trees lay broken

indicators.note: something broken is smashed into bits, which can be put back in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gale has left the trees lying smashed on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The storm in the surface supplies the definition; 'broken' looks like part of the damage but works on the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: An easterly is a wind blowing from the east, so it names one particular kind of breeze.
